parameters.deformation: thickness 15 mm to 10 mm, then to 5 mm at 800 °C

evidence.quote: (i) The 15-mm thick alloy plates were first heated to 1100 °C at a heating rate of ∼30 °C/s and hot rolled to 10 mm, and then thinned to 5 mm at 800 °C to refine the coarse grain of the homogenized alloys and produce Laves submicron precipitates, followed by AC to room temperature (RT).
(ii) The 5 mm-thick alloy plates underwent 300 °C WR with 70% thickness reduction to further refine the layered grain obtained by HR but also introduce more substructures such as dislocation cells.

(iii) The WR samples experienced FA to 1150 °C at the heating rate ∼100 °C/s for ∼3 s to promote RX and regression of Laves precipitates obtained in the HR process, followed by water quenching (WQ) to RT.

(iv) To enhance the density of nucleation sites of Laves nanoprecipitates and promote their uniform distribution in grain interiors during aging, 15% pre-rolling at RT was applied to the alloys to introduce more nucleation sites (e.g. dislocations) before aging with the thickness reduction to ∼1.25 mm.
The aging treatment at 600 °C for 1 h was finally performed, followed by AC to RT, rendering a high density of Laves nanoprecipitates prepared uniformly in grain interiors.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Grain sizes of the RFPA samples
evidence.quote: Obviously, fine equiaxed ferrite grains bounded by high angle GBs (HAGBs, > 15 °) have been prepared successfully as compared with the C-RR samples. By measuring more than 100 grains based on the linear interception method, the average grain sizes of 0Si-, 0.5Si-, 1Si-, and 2Si-alloys were obtained to be ∼10.3, ∼10.1, ∼8.2, and ∼5.6 μm, respectively, which is only 1/15 to 1/4 of those of C-RR samples.
